newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Demasz, Edasz top Hungary electricity firms - MC Sec.
newsitem.headline: Demasz, Edasz top Hungary electricity firms - MC Sec.

text.p: Fundamentals and regional advantages make Demasz and Edasz Hungary's best performing regional electricity suppliers, according to an analyst report by MC Securities.

"Edasz supplies Hungary's strongest growth region near the Austrian border and recent changes in tariffs lead us to believe that the company will show strong results in the near term," analyst Julie Quist said.
Edasz in 1995 posted a loss of 2.43 billion forints on net sales of 34.69 billion forints, while 1996 figures are not yet available.
MC Securities' other favourite, Demasz, was already profitable in 1995.
"Demasz is extremely strong on fundamentals and its sound management made it the only profitable electricity distributor company in 1995," she said.

In 1995 Demasz generated a net profit of 125.8 million forints on net sales of 19.51 billion. "Demasz expects a small profit again for 1996 and is likely to pay out a dividend for that year," Quist said.
"We believe that the two companies will outperform their sector over the next two to three years," she concluded.
The analyst report said strategic investors in the Hungarian electricity utilities would see the desired eight percent return in two years' time.

The government announced last November retail hikes for distributors of 24.9 percent for electricity and 18.8 percent for gas but did not define the margins which would be granted to energy producers and distributors.
The margins mean an increase in prices that distributors have to pay for the energy they sell to their consumers of around 18.3 percent for electricity and 16.9 percent for gas.

"Tariffs remain a matter of great controversy in Hungary since, according to the strategic investors, tariffs still fall short of generating the eight percent return on equity promised by the government prior to the privatisation," Quist said.
Hungary sold minority stakes in six regional distributors to strategic investors in 1995.
